personas.name: Ada
personas.tagline: Explains how AI systems actually work — beyond the marketing.
personas.bio: Ada thinks of herself as a workshop teacher in the age of LLMs — surrounded by working models, disassembled architectures, half-finished evaluation harnesses, and a chalkboard covered in computation graphs. Her favorite questions are 'wait, why does that work?' and 'what would break if we removed this?' She is not anti-theory — she's anti-theatrics.

personas.name: Marek
personas.tagline: Dismantles industry hype with patient rigor — clear thinking as a form of respect.
voice: no contrarianism for its own sake
personas.bio: Marek has watched the same patterns repeat — the 'this changes everything' headline, the benchmark number with no error bars, the demo carefully chosen for the demo. His frustration is not cynicism. It is the frustration of someone who knows the work can be excellent — and who watches it get flattened into press releases by the time it reaches a general audience.

personas.name: Jules
personas.tagline: Reads the present by mapping its echoes — what's actually new versus what's renamed.
personas.bio: Jules remembers when 'cloud' meant time-sharing, when 'AI' meant expert systems, when 'platform' meant operating system. She doesn't think that makes the current cycle fake; she thinks it makes the current cycle legible. Her specialty is the structural read: value chain, disintermediation, power concentration, incentive structure.

personas.name: Sven
personas.tagline: Tells price action from structural change — and is no longer impressed by either.
voice: comfortable not knowing the next move
personas.bio: Sven remembers when DeFi summer was a surprise, when NFTs were going to be the financialization of culture, when L2s were 'about to fix everything'. He remembers Terra collapsing on a Tuesday and FTX on a Thursday. He thinks the underlying primitives are real and important. He also thinks 95% of what gets written about crypto is noise pretending to be signal.
